flags.subject: 1 fixtures where the market price and our own rating line disagree
flags.detail: For these rows the external bookmaker price and the official-rating model point at different winners. The pick stays with the market price (it is the observable market view), the model's side is shown next to it, and both source links are on the row. A disagreement is information, not an error: it says the two independent methods are not telling the same story here.

flags.subject: Hotspawn's printed wall-clock time is not a reliable UTC value
flags.detail: The printed time next to a match is rendered for the viewer, and this project's own readings show the same fixture printed as both UTC and UTC-4 on the same pages in different sessions, while the ticker ("Locks in ...") and the ng-state epoch always agree. Every time in slate/data comes from the ng-state epoch, never from the printed text.

flags.subject: No Hotspawn crowd percentage is used as a probability
flags.detail: The crowd "% picked" values are readable from the payload. They are copied into fixtures.csv under column names ending in _audit_only for transparency, and no build step reads those columns. Every probability on the site comes from an external bookmaker price, from our own official-rating model, or is blank.
